text:
ashley: Quick postmortem follow-up for Meridian — putting the action list and owners here. Root cause summary: repeated VPC peering route flaps induced reconnect storms on the on-prem edge, which then caused NAT ephemeral port exhaustion and isolation of dedicated pods.

devon: ok. i'll take the NAT scaling + conntrack/ephemeral tuning. need confirmation on peak concurrent 5-tuple count. @natalie-pm can you paste numbers?

natalie-pm: Meridian reported ~800 steady flows, but nightly batch jobs spike to ~2.4k for ~3-6m windows. they run between 01:00-01:30 UTC.

samir: i'll own the peering side — propose: increase BGP hold-time, enable route-flap damping, and add a pre-filter for suspicious prefix churn. planning patch for config templates.

kevin: i'll own the onprem test harness + canary. plan: simulate reconnect storms with 2x, 5x batch loads to measure NAT exhaustion behavior. target: reproduce in staging vpc-onprem replica.

ashley: thanks. adding concise action tracker below. will create Jira REQ-5234 and link here.

ops-bot: Jira REQ-5234 created and linked to thread. Assigned watchers: ashley, devon, samir, kevin, natalie-pm.

ashley: ``
ACTIONS:
- ACTION-001 | Owner: devon | Due: 2026-04-02 | Fix: extend ephemeral port range + conntrack tuning on customer gateway | Status: open
- ACTION-002 | Owner: samir | Due: 2026-03-30 | Fix: BGP hold-time increase + route-flap damping on peering router | Status: open
- ACTION-003 | Owner: kevin | Due: 2026-04-07 | Canary test for reconnect storm scaling and NAT behavior | Status: todo
- ACTION-004 | Owner: ashley | Due: 2026-03-28 | Run regression eval against prefix-churn testset + alert thresholds | Status: in progress
- ACTION-005 | Owner: natalie-pm | Due: 2026-04-05 | Customer comms + schedule maintenance window for gateway changes | Status: pending
``

devon: config snippet for conntrack adjustments (quick prototype):
```
# increase conntrack table size and timeout
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288
sysctl -w net.ipv4.netfilter.ip_conntrack_max=524288
# ephemeral port range
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="15000 61000"
```

samir: for peering i suggest starting with hold-time 180 and flap damping with half-life 300. will open a PR against infra-configs.

kevin: scheduling the canary. rough plan:
- day0: replicate peak flows in staging
- day1: run scaling tests, collect conntrack metrics
- day2: validate mitigation knobs and rollback plan

natalie-pm: I'll draft the customer note — propose maintenance window 2026-04-03 02:00-04:00 UTC. any objections? :calendar:

devon: no objections. :+1:

ashley: let's do a 10min standup each morning at 09:00 PT until all ACTIONs are closed. I'll post a short status update each day here.

ops-bot: Standup reminder scheduled for 2026-03-26 through 2026-04-10 at 09:00 PT.

kevin: one more note — we saw a pattern: customers with long-lived keepalive-less TCP sessions are more vulnerable. can we add a monitoring eval that counts long-lived non-KA sessions > 120s?

ashley: good call. ACTION-006 created: Owner: ashley | Due: 2026-03-29 | Add detection rule for long-lived non-keepalive sessions and alert runbook | Status: open

samir: I'll include a short doc describing when to enable route-flap damping per customer (thresholds + rollback).

natalie-pm: i'll sync with customer on business impact and prioritize downtime window.

ashley: thanks everyone — will update REQ-5234 with config links and next steps after today's standup. :white_check_mark:
